meaning: to work or study late into the night
example: I had to burn the midnight oil to finish my report before the meeting.
origin: Comes from the time before electric light, when people worked or read by oil lamps late at night

wrong_meanings.why_wrong: The idiom has nothing to do with spending money; it describes working late.

wrong_meanings.meaning: to set fire to a building
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: 'Burn' in this idiom is not about fire or destruction; it refers to the lamp burning oil.

wrong_meanings.meaning: to go to bed very early
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: This is the opposite of the idiom, which describes staying awake and working late.

explanation: 'Burn the midnight oil' means to work or study late at night. It comes from the time when oil lamps were used for light, so the lamp kept burning while the person kept working.
